title: Streaming-to-async embeddings importer with backpressure & de-duplication
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Provide a developer-friendly ingestion path that accepts high-throughput streaming inputs and reliably converts them to async batch embedding jobs with strong guarantees: at-least-once delivery with transparent de-duplication via client-provided idempotency keys, deterministic retry semantics, and backpressure signals to source clients. This ticket encompasses API surface design (stream+batch hybrid), server-side orchestration (checkpointing, job creation), storage & checkpoint format, retry & dedupe algorithm, and ops observability (per-job metrics, failure reasons, SLA alerts).

Scope:
- New streaming ingestion endpoint that accepts NDJSON lines and returns an ingest session handle.
- Session server-side buffering with adaptive backpressure (reject vs pause signaling) based on in-flight token/seq estimates.
- When session reaches thresholds, it triggers an async batch create job in the existing bulk importer queue with a canonical job payload.
- Idempotency: Accept client idempotency-key per document and a session-level idempotency-token for dedup across retries and reconnects.
- Exactly-once visible semantics for downstream vector databases: dedupe before final commit using monotonic checkpoints and short-term dedupe cache (redis) + content-hash fallback.
- Retry model: client receives per-document status in session events; server supports exponential backoff retries for transient embedding compute failures and exposes failure reasons for operational triage.
- Admin tools: console view for ingest sessions, ability to cancel/flush sessions, re-run failed batches, and export session-level logs.

Non-goals: synchronous single-request bulk upload (covered by existing bulk API), client-side chunking libraries (we'll provide examples).
design_notes:
We considered two approaches for deduplication: (A) Strict idempotency table (global write-once record keyed by client_key+content-hash) which is strongest but adds write amplification and operational complexity; (B) Session-local monotonic checkpoints with a short TTL dedupe cache (redis) plus content-hash checks on final commit. Chosen: hybrid (B) to balance cost and correctness for high-throughput customers.

Batch sizing heuristics: trigger job when either: total documents >= 10k OR total tokens >= 5M OR session duration >= 60s. Use sample-based token estimator on streaming input to avoid O(n) tokenization.

Backpressure: expose HTTP 429 with Retry-After when queue or memory thresholds crossed. Also support server-sent events (SSE) for long-lived sessions to communicate progress and per-document verdicts.

Persistence: session manifest persisted to blobstore with versioned schema v1. Checkpoint records include sequence number, client_id, document_id, idempotency_key, and status.

Telemetry: per-session metrics (ingest_rate, queued_docs, avg_latency_ms, dedupe_rate, fail_rate) and job-level telemetry forwarded to Console. Alerts: fail_rate > 2% and queue_wait_ms > 500ms -> paging for P0s.
acceptance_criteria: API: New POST /v1/embeddings/stream-ingest starts a session and returns session_id and websocket/SSE URL for events.
Correctness: Documents with identical idempotency_key within session or within dedupe window are de-duplicated; duplicates return canonical document_id in event stream.
Durability: Session manifest persisted and recoverable after a host restart without data loss for sessions in 'open' state.
Scaling: Produce sustained ingest at 3k docs/sec per session cluster with median per-doc latency under 80ms until batch trigger.
Retries: Transient embedding compute failures are retried automatically up to 5 attempts with exponential backoff; persistent failures surfaced and plumbed to re-run tooling.
Observability: Console shows sessions, queued sizes, and per-job failure reasons; SLO dashboards updated with ingest latency and dedupe metrics.
Safety: Rate limiting and backpressure enforce memory and queue thresholds to avoid OOMs.
Docs & SDKs: Node + Python examples for streaming client and recommended retry/idempotency patterns published in docs.
E2E test: Simulated client reconnects and duplicate message replay do not create duplicate final vectors (end-to-end vector counts stable).
updates: 2026-03-01: Spike completed—prototype for SSE session shows stable event delivery under 500 rps. (PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4821)
2026-03-04: Design review with infra—decided on hybrid dedupe approach using redis LRU cache + checkpoint manifest. Added TTL considerations to design notes.
2026-03-07: Implemented session manifest schema v1 in blobstore; added migration script for older importers to annotate source-job mapping. (PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4898)
2026-03-10: Load test with synthetic payloads reached 2.8k docs/sec before backpressure; identified hot-spot in token-estimator CPU path—assigned optimization task ENG-67210.
2026-03-12: First internal dogfood run with sample customer dataset; observed 0.8% transient compute failures retried successfully.
comments: Miguel Torres (2026-03-02): Left a comment on the PR—we should add per-doc size limits to avoid huge single-record spikes (see design_notes).
Priya Shah (Prod, 2026-03-05): Need clear guidance in docs about recommended idempotency key semantics; suggested example keys "user-id:source:dedupe-hash".
SRE (2026-03-08): Concern about redis dedupe cache becoming a single point of failure—requested fallback mode that continues ingest with increased dedupe window and adds a warning in console.
Ethan Cole (Security, 2026-03-09): Reviewed payload retention—requested encryption-at-rest for session manifests and KMS annotation (added to TODOs).
